WTA Finals in Indian Wells: Format, schedule, players, as Elena Rybakina and Aryna Sabalenka lead field at end-of-season event
The season-ending championship heads to Indian Wells for the first time, with new world No 1 Elena Rybakina leading the field along with Aryna Sabalenka and Coco Gauff; You can watch the WTA Finals live on Sky Sports from 8-15 November
Tuesday 3 November 2026 23:58, UK
Defending champion Elena Rybakina leads the field at Indian Wells for the WTA Finals - live on Sky Sports from 8-15 November.
The crown jewel of women's tennis takes place in Indian Wells, California with eight singles players and doubles teams having qualified in the Race to the Finals competing for tennis' ultimate prize.
Matches are played in a round-robin format between two groups of four, with the top two players or teams from each group moving on to the knockout stage.
- Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
- Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW📱

WTA Finals: Meet the players
Elena Rybakina
The 27-year-old arrives in the California desert as the world No 1 after bringing an end to Sabalenka's 99-week reign at the top. She captured both the Australian Open and the US Open - defeating rival Sabalenka in both finals.
2026 record: 49-14
Titles: 3 (Australian Open, Stuttgart, US Open)
Previous WTA Finals appearances: 3
Best result: Champion (2025)
Aryna Sabalenka
The Belarusian remains Rybakina's biggest threat after sweeping to victory at Indian Wells and Miami - becoming just the fifth woman in WTA history to complete the 'Sunshine Double'.
2026 record: 47-10
Titles: 3 (Brisbane, Indian Wells, Miami)
Previous WTA Finals appearances: 5
Best result: Finalist (2022, 2025)
Coco Gauff
The American has all the momentum following a sensational second half of the year, highlighted by a title in Cincinnati and semi-final runs at both Wimbledon and the US Open.
2026 record: 47-15
Titles: 1 (Cincinnati)
Previous WTA Finals appearances: 4
Best result: Champion (2024)
Mirra Andreeva
Three players will be making their tournament debuts with Andreeva leading the newcomers after securing her first Grand Slam title at the French Open.
2026 record: 50-16
Titles: 3 (Adelaide, Linz, Roland Garros)
Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0
Karolina Muchova
Her victory at the WTA 1000 event in Doha in February was just the second title of her career and her first since 2019. She then won a grass-court title in Bad Homburg before reaching her second Grand Slam final at Wimbledon in the summer.
2026 record: 40-11
Titles: 2 (Doha, Bad Homburg)
Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0
Linda Noskova
The reigning Wimbledon champion also reached the semi-finals at Indian Wells earlier in the year and advanced to the US Open quarter-finals in September.
2026 record: 35-15
Titles: 2 (Berlin, Wimbledon)
Previous WTA Finals appearances: 0
Jessica Pegula
American Pegula reached 50 victories as well as making five finals, including titles in Dubai and Charleston before finishing runner-up in Berlin, Washington DC and Cincinnati. She also reached the US Open semi-finals for a second consecutive year and made the quarter-finals at Wimbledon and Rome.
2026 record: 50-13
Titles: 2 (Dubai, Charleston)
Previous WTA Finals appearances: 4
Best result: Finalist (2023)
Elina Svitolina
Svitolina is heading back to the season-ending event seven years after her last appearance. She went undefeated to win the title in 2018 and reached the final again a year later.
2026 record: 46-14
Titles: 2 (Auckland, Rome)
Previous WTA Finals appearances: 3
Best result: Champion (2018)
Keys joins Sky Sports team
Former Australian Open champion Madison Keys will join Sky Sports' broadcasting team with the 31-year-old offering viewers an insider's perspective as a commentator and analyst alongside Martina Navratilova, Marion Bartoli, commentator Jonathan Overend and Laura Robson.
Keys, who lifted the Daphne Akhurst Memorial Cup in 2025, remains an active competitor on the WTA Tour.
She won the Eastbourne title in June 2026 and reached the third round of the US Open in September. She is currently ranked No 24 in the world.
WTA Finals 2026: Full schedule
Play begins at 8pm each day.
- Sunday 8 November: Round-robin matches
- Monday 9 November: Round-robin matches
- Tuesday 10 November: Round-robin matches
- Wednesday 11 November: Round-robin matches
- Thursday 12 November: Round-robin matches
- Friday 13 November: Round-robin matches
- Saturday 14 November: Semifinals
- Sunday 15 November: Finals
When is the Order of Play released?
The Order of Play is typically released the evening prior to each day of competition.
Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App. You can watch the WTA Finals live on Sky Sports from 8-15 November.
